data.reasoning: Both models reviewed the same three files (.gitignore, .SRCINFO, PKGBUILD). The PKGBUILD downloads from the official InteractiveBrokers domain (download2.interactivebrokers.com) with a pinned SHA-512 checksum, uses standard Install4j installer patterns in prepare()/package(), and performs no network operations or code execution outside the build environment. The .SRCINFO correctly reflects the PKGBUILD metadata. The .gitignore is a standard file listing build artifacts. The only disagreement stems from qwen3-235b experiencing an API error (HTTP 400) when auditing .gitignore, which is a non-executable metadata file with zero security relevance. Deepseek-v4-flash successfully audited all files and correctly identified the package as safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is purely technical: qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed with an API error (BadRequestError) when attempting to audit .gitignore, resulting in an INCONCLUSIVE file verdict that propagated to the overall result. Deepseek-v4-flash successfully audited the same .gitignore file and correctly identified it as a standard, benign file. The .gitignore file cannot execute code or pose any security risk, so the API failure should not have resulted in an inconclusive package verdict.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed to audit .gitignore due to LLM API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: When a model fails to audit a non-executable, non-security-sensitive file (like .gitignore) due to a transient API error, the tool should not propagate that failure to an INCONCLUSIVE package verdict if other files were successfully audited and found safe.

The audit tool should distinguish between coverage failures on security-critical files (PKGBUILD, .install, patches) vs. non-critical files (.gitignore, README, editor configs) when determining overall verdict confidence.
Models should be instructed that .gitignore and similar metadata files are inherently safe and do not require deep security analysis - a simple pattern match would suffice.
